synthesis: DEV-2575 reports that Scout field users who forget their password have no recovery mechanism, and admins cannot reset passwords for verified users. VERIFIED: Scout PWA uses email+password auth (resources/js/clarity-scout/views/Login.vue:23-58 → app/Http/Controllers/Api/ClarityScoutAuthController:21-87). Clarity main panel uses OTP/passwordless auth (app/Filament/Auth/CustomLoginPage → app/Filament/Auth/OneTimePassword, implemented in prior Clarity OTP work). Scout currently has NO forgot-password or password-reset routes/controllers (routes/web.php:104-113 only contains set-password for onboarding at line 108, and force-login for admin impersonation at line 105). The admin resend_onboarding action (app/Filament/Resources/ScoutUsersResource.php:356-412) ONLY works when email_verified_at IS NULL (line 368 guard), so it covers pre-onboarding only — once a user completes onboarding (sets password + verifies email via app/Http/Controllers/Auth/ScoutSetPasswordController:35-41), the resend button disappears and there is NO recovery path. Force-login (app/Http/Controllers/ClarityScoutForceLoginController:14-54) is admin impersonation requiring session('admin_impersonator') and does NOT provide self-serve recovery. The ticket proposes two solutions: (A) admin-side password reset/recovery link, (B) magic-link/passwordless like Clarity (PREFERRED per ticket). AC1 contains a logical contradiction: 'recovery that does NOT require remembering email' is impossible for email-based magic-link (magic-link REQUIRES knowing the email to send to). The ticket must clarify whether the real ask is (a) forgotten password with known email (solvable via OTP or reset link), or (b) forgotten email itself (requires out-of-band identifier like phone number or admin search by name/kit). The pwd_reset_tokens_table table EXISTS (database/migrations/0001_01_01_000000_create_users_table:25-29) but is unused.

scope.summary: Convert Scout PWA to OTP/passwordless (preferred), OR add admin-assisted password-reset that works post-verification. Both paths require auth flow changes (Scout API, PWA UI, middleware or OTP classes), admin UI (ScoutUsersResource recovery action), tests, and notifications. AC1 contradiction (recovery without email vs magic-link requiring email) MUST be resolved before scoping. If OTP: Scout login becomes 2-step (email → OTP → token), aligns with Clarity, reuses OneTimePassword/OneTimePasswordNotification. If password-reset: new signed-URL route similar to set-password but bypasses email_verified_at guard. No database schema changes needed. Not scale-relevant (auth UX).

Ticket must clarify: (a) forgotten password with known email (solvable via OTP or reset link, aligns with PREFERRED magic-link solution), or (b) forgotten email itself (requires out-of-band identifier like phone or admin lookup by name/kit). Implementation path depends on clarification.

If password-reset path chosen: follows ScoutOnboardingNotification/ValidateScoutSignedUrl/ScoutSetPasswordController precedent (app/Notifications/ScoutOnboardingNotification:24-45, app/Http/Middleware/ValidateScoutSignedUrl:20-33, app/Http/Controllers/Auth/ScoutSetPasswordController:66-84). questions.q: AC1 says 'recovery that does NOT require remembering email' but preferred solution is 'magic-link' which REQUIRES email to send to — is the real ask (a) forgotten password with known email (solvable via OTP or reset link), or (b) forgotten email itself (requires alternate identifier like phone or admin name/kit lookup)?
questions.derivation: AC contradiction detected at acceptance_criteria analysis; magic-link fundamentally requires knowing recipient email address (app/Notifications/ScoutOnboardingNotification:38-42 shows URL sent via email, app/Notifications/OneTimePasswordNotification:29-41 shows OTP sent via email). If email is forgotten, alternate identifier needed (phone, kit serial, admin search by driver name). This is NOT a tech question — it is product scope clarification that determines whether solution is (a) standard email-based recovery flows (OTP or reset link, both existing patterns), or (b) alternate-identifier lookup system (fundamentally different scope, no precedent).

questions.q: Which path is approved: (A) convert Scout to OTP/passwordless like Clarity main panel (PREFERRED per ticket summary, larger change but aligns auth flows), or (B) add password-reset flow keeping current password login (simpler, less disruptive to Scout PWA UX)?
questions.derivation: Ticket summary says 'magic-link / OTP like Clarity' is PREFERRED, but password-reset is listed as alternative. Both satisfy AC2/3/4 but have different implementation scope: OTP requires rewriting Scout login flow (resources/js/clarity-scout/views/Login.vue:23-58, app/Http/Controllers/Api/ClarityScoutAuthController:21-87) to match Clarity CustomLoginPage two-step pattern (email submit → OTP sent → OTP verify → token), plus admin recovery action. Password-reset keeps existing password login intact, only adds forgot-password link + signed-URL reset endpoints + admin recovery action. OTP has larger code surface (PWA UI change, API flow change, testing both paths) but eliminates password management burden long-term. Decision affects file list, test strategy, and QA scope.

questions.q: Does Scout need self-serve 'Forgot Password?' UI in PWA Login.vue, or is admin-only recovery sufficient per AC2?
questions.derivation: AC1 mentions 'self-serve mechanism' but AC2 only requires 'admin can assist'. If admin-only: no PWA UI changes needed (only ScoutUsersResource action at lines 356-412). If self-serve: PWA needs 'Forgot Password?' link (resources/js/clarity-scout/views/Login.vue:47 below password field) linking to either (a) OTP flow (conditional OTP field after email submit), or (b) new ForgotPassword.vue view that accepts email and shows 'Check your email' confirmation. Admin-only is simpler but less user-friendly for field drivers with no admin contact available.

questions.q: If password-reset path chosen: should reset-password signed URL reuse same 7-day TTL and one-shot pattern as set-password (app/Notifications/ScoutOnboardingNotification:17 linkTtlDays=7, app/Http/Controllers/Auth/ScoutSetPasswordController:68-73 email_verified_at guard makes it one-shot), or allow multiple uses / different TTL?
questions.derivation: Onboarding link is one-shot because email_verified_at is NULL on first use and set after success (app/Http/Controllers/Auth/ScoutSetPasswordController:39-41), making the link invalid for subsequent attempts (line 71 guard). Password-reset for already-verified user cannot use same guard — needs different mechanism. Options: (a) use pwd_reset_tokens_table table (database/migrations/0001_01_01_000000_create_users_table:25-29, standard Laravel password reset pattern, token consumed on use), (b) allow multiple uses within TTL (simpler but security tradeoff if link leaked), or (c) tie to user.updated_at or user.password hash so link invalidates after first successful reset. Standard Laravel pattern (a) is safest precedent.

blockers.description: AC1 requires 'recovery WITHOUT remembering email' but proposed solution 'magic-link / OTP' fundamentally REQUIRES email. This is not a tech question — it is product scope clarification.
